scope: UK educational teaching surface. Opened only after Money Decision 101 INVESTING_READINESS.

nodes.label: Investing
nodes.definition: Putting money into assets with the aim of receiving a return over time. Values can rise or fall. There is no risk-free investment.
nodes.firstPrinciple: This page teaches the idea of investing. It does not say investing is suitable for you.

nodes.label: Review debt
nodes.definition: Short-term debt should generally be prioritised before investing. Do not use credit to invest.
nodes.firstPrinciple: Debt review is an ordering rule, not a list of which debt to pay first.

nodes.label: Emergency savings
nodes.definition: Keep accessible emergency savings before committing money to investments.
nodes.firstPrinciple: This page explains that a buffer comes before investing education. It does not set your personal buffer size.

nodes.label: Workplace pension
nodes.pageSection: Start with your financial foundations; UK accounts and pensions
nodes.definition: If you are employed, consider your workplace pension as part of your foundations. Schemes often receive employer contributions and invest for retirement. Check your own scheme rules.
nodes.firstPrinciple: Generic contribution examples are not your contribution recommendation.

nodes.label: Time horizon
nodes.definition: Money needed soon is different from long-term money. MoneyHelper discusses investing as longer-term, including goals more than five years away. The FCA notes that for a fairly short timeframe, perhaps up to three years, savings may be more appropriate to explore.
nodes.firstPrinciple: Three years and five years are educational guideposts, not a personal suitability test.

nodes.label: Risk
nodes.definition: Investment values can fall as well as rise. Understand how much loss you could tolerate while still meeting your goals.
nodes.firstPrinciple: Naming risk is not a regulated risk-profile or a recommendation to take risk.

nodes.label: Diversification
nodes.definition: Spreading exposure across different assets and markets can reduce reliance on any single investment. It cannot remove investment risk.
nodes.firstPrinciple: Diversification is a concept, not an asset-allocation recipe.

nodes.label: Costs
nodes.definition: Investment and service-provider fees reduce the returns you keep. Upfront and ongoing costs are part of comparing options.
nodes.firstPrinciple: This page does not quantify a '1% fee costs hundreds of thousands' claim.

nodes.label: Individual Savings Account
nodes.definition: ISAs can hold cash or eligible investments and provide tax advantages. A Stocks and Shares ISA is a tax wrapper, not a guarantee that holdings will make money.
nodes.firstPrinciple: A wrapper changes tax treatment. It does not remove investment risk or name a provider.

nodes.label: Promised high or guaranteed returns
nodes.definition: Be cautious of promotions that promise very high or guaranteed returns or present investing as a quick way to get rich. Understand the risks before committing money.
nodes.firstPrinciple: This is a caution, not a claim that any promotion is a scam.

never: A named security, fund, provider, or portfolio allocation
A statement that investing is personally suitable
Guaranteed return, guaranteed profit, or 'the best time was yesterday'
US account types such as 401(k) or IRA
Sending people back through Money Decision as if that were how to enter this page
Implying FCA, MoneyHelper, or GOV.UK endorse Nexus Motivus
outOfScopeV1: FSCS protection (named as a future downstream topic in Money Decision evidence, not taught on this page yet)
S&P 500 as a thing to own
ETF or tracker as a v1 node until tracker/passive evidence is added

namedInstrumentTiers.rule: A vehicle type may become a node. A ticker may not.
namedInstrumentTiers.needsEvidence: New evidence ID. FCA 'Advantages of mainstream investments' explains tracker/passive funds. That page is not in the Investing 101 registry yet.
namedInstrumentTiers.mustNot: Name a provider, ticker, or 'start with an ETF'.

namedInstrumentTiers.rule: Explain matching an index vs trying to beat one. Do not pick the index.
namedInstrumentTiers.needsEvidence: Same FCA tracker/passive page. This page already removed 'A low-cost total market index fund is a great starting point for most people.'
namedInstrumentTiers.mustNot: Recommend a global tracker, total-market fund, or any named fund.

namedInstrumentTiers.rule: Named US index. Not a concept in this UK beginner graph.
namedInstrumentTiers.needsEvidence: None. If a later lesson illustrates what an index is, FCA already uses the UK FTSE 100 as an example of a market index, not as a product to buy.
namedInstrumentTiers.mustNot: Teach 'buy the S&P 500' or treat that index as the default portfolio.

namedInstrumentTiers.rule: Property vehicle. Different lesson from diversification, not a buy list.
namedInstrumentTiers.needsEvidence: A GOV.UK, FCA, or MoneyHelper REIT/property-investment page. Not in the current Investing 101 citations.
namedInstrumentTiers.mustNot: Frame REITs as a yield product or a substitute for reviewing a workplace pension.
